\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

definitions.name: finite-tail-attractor adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(m\), \(\bar\eta_1,\ldots,\bar\eta_m\), \(s_\eta\), \(p_-\), \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}vanishing\text{-}modulus}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T\) to be the set of laws \(P\) that, at horizon \(T\), satisfy every condition in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) with these common objects, envelopes, and moduli. The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). Thus \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), every one of the \(m\) separated basins has mass at least \(p_-\), the policy path is approximated by its selected attractor only through the uniform Cesaro inequality, and the associated attraction error satisfies \(r_T+\delta_T\to0\). Pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is not imposed.

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-state separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, define \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J=J-1\), and put \(\eta_t=\eta_\infty\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: terminal-representative covariance
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
For every \(j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 p_j=P(J=j),\qquad
 \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j),\qquad
 V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Omega_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}\Omega_j,\qquad
 V_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}V_j,
\]
and set
\[
 \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty),\qquad
 V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), substitution of \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction:
Set
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\}.
\]
Define the total nonnegative scalar
\[
 \widehat q_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,
   &\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\
 0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,
 \end{cases}
\]
where the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and set
\[
 \mathcal E_T(c)=\mathcal H_T\cap\{\widehat q_T(c)\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\}.
\]
Define the total early-scale event-truncated sandwich by
\[
 \widehat V_T(c)=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top},
   &\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c),\\
 I_d,&\text{on }\mathcal E_T(c)^c.
 \end{cases}
\]
Thus every inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal H_T\), and \(c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c>0\) for every realization because \(c\ne0\).

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale realized-QV Wald pivot
definitions.construction:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich \(\widehat V_T(c)\) and define the everywhere finite statistic
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)=
 \frac{\sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)}
 {\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c}}.
\]
The denominator is positive on every realization by the construction of \(\widehat V_T(c)\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction:
Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for the current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is
\[
q_a^+=\frac{q_a}{1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2},\qquad
\beta_a^+=\frac{\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a)}{1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2}.
\]
The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. Put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(C_{t,a}=\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}\), and, for \(t\geq1\),
\[
\Psi_t=\left(\frac{D_{t,1}}t,\frac{D_{t,2}}t,\frac{N_{t,1}}t,\frac{N_{t,2}}t\right),\qquad
U_{t+1}=\bigl(C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}^2,C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}^2,
C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(1),C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(2)\bigr).
\]
With \(\gamma_t=1/t\), the sufficient-statistic updates give the exact recursion
\[
\Psi_{t+1}-\Psi_t=\gamma_{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t)=\frac1{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t).
\]

Here is the actual one-step finite expectation under the bounded law in Definition~\(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\). Let \(\mu_1=1/2\), \(\mu_2=1/12\), let \(p_{t,1}(1)=u_t\), \(p_{t,1}(-4)=v_t\), and let \(p_{t,2}(x)=1-p_{t,1}(x)\). Conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\), independence and equiprobability of \(X_{t+1}\) and the innovations \(R_{t+1,a}\) give the finite law
\[
\operatorname{guoXuNoiseLaw}_t(x,a,r_1,r_2)
=\frac18p_{t,a}(x),
\quad x\in\{-4,1\},\quad a\in\{1,2\},\quad r_1,r_2\in\{-1,1\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal U(x,a,r_1,r_2)=
\bigl(\mathbf1\{a=1\}x^2,\mathbf1\{a=2\}x^2,
\mathbf1\{a=1\}x(\mu_1+\sigma_1r_1),
\mathbf1\{a=2\}x(\mu_2+\sigma_2r_2)\bigr).
\]
Thus the conditional expectation is the displayed finite sum
\[
E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]
=\sum_{x\in\{-4,1\}}\sum_{a=1}^2\sum_{r_1,r_2\in\{-1,1\}}
\operatorname{guoXuNoiseLaw}_t(x,a,r_1,r_2)\mathcal U(x,a,r_1,r_2)
=h(u_t,v_t),
\]
where
\[
h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
\frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
Let
\[
M_{t+1}=U_{t+1}-E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t],
\qquad
R_{j,k}=\sum_{s=j}^k\gamma_{s+1}M_{s+1}\quad(j\leq k).
\]
For every coordinate \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\), every \(\epsilon>0\), and every initialized law \(P_{\eta_0}\), the coordinatewise dyadic tail estimate proved in equation (12) is
\[
P_{\eta_0}\!\left\{\exists\ell\geq L:\ 
\sup_{k\geq2^\ell}\left|R_{2^\ell,k}^{(i)}\right|>\epsilon\right\}
\leq \frac{C_i}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{\ell\geq L}2^{-\ell}
\longrightarrow0\qquad(L\to\infty),
\]
for a finite constant \(C_i\) depending only on the fixed bounded-noise envelope.

For \(C<\infty\) and \(c>0\), define the compact carrier
\[
\mathsf K(C,c)=[c,C]^2\times[-C,C]^2.
\]
For the recursion above one may take
\[
c_{\mathrm{GX}}=\frac{17}{400},\qquad
C_{\mathrm{GX}}=\max\left\{17,1+4\max\left\{\frac12+\sigma_1,\frac1{12}+\sigma_2\right\}\right\};
\]
then \(\Psi_t\in\mathsf K(C_{\mathrm{GX}},c_{\mathrm{GX}})\) eventually almost surely. Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), \(h_2=h(q,q)\), and, for \(\psi=(d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\in\mathsf K(C,c)\), put \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\). The exact four-mode convexified graph on this carrier is
\[
F_{C,c}(\psi)=
\begin{cases}
\{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
\{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
\end{cases}
\]
Its graph is understood in the relative topology of \(\mathsf K(C,c)\times\mathbb R^4\); it is relatively closed there and has nonempty compact convex values. No ambient closed-graph assertion at the boundary of \(\{d_1,d_2>0\}\) is part of this handle. The name \(\operatorname{GuoXuReductionConditions}(C,c)\) denotes only: the exact recursion above; eventual containment in \(\mathsf K(C,c)\); the relative closed-graph and compact-convex-value properties just stated; the switching-layer drift inclusion
\[
E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]-\Psi_t\in F_{C,c}^{\,c_0t^{-1/2}}(\Psi_t)
\]
for some finite deterministic \(c_0\) and all sufficiently large \(t\); boundedness of \(U_{t+1}\) and \(\Psi_t\); and the displayed coordinatewise dyadic tail limit for \(R_{j,k}\).

For clarity, the compact-initial-set finite-attractor property is only a named target for future work. For \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\geq1\), distinct deterministic targets \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_1,\ldots,\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\geq1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable selector \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\), define
\[
B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\},
\qquad
\mathcal L_{\eta_0}=\left\{\lim_{t\to\infty}
(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
=\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\right\}.
\]
For a compact set
\[
K_0\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}
\operatorname{relint}_{\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j),
\]
define the event
\[
\mathcal A_T(\eta_0,K_0)=\left\{
\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T
\left\|(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
-\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\right\|_2
\leq r_T(K_0)\right\}.
\]
For nonnegative deterministic sequences \(r_T(K_0)\) and \(\delta_T(K_0)\), the future predicate \(\operatorname{CompactAttraction}_{\mathrm{GX}}(K_0)\) means
\[
P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_{\eta_0})=1\quad\text{for every }\eta_0\in K_0,
\qquad
\sup_{\eta_0\in K_0}P_{\eta_0}\{\mathcal A_T(\eta_0,K_0)^c\}
\leq\delta_T(K_0),
\qquad
r_T(K_0)\to0,\quad\delta_T(K_0)\to0.
\]
This future predicate is not asserted by this definition or by the present dynamics theorem, and it is not a conjunct of \(\operatorname{GuoXuReductionConditions}(C,c)\). In particular, the handle posits neither a quantitative-hitting condition, nor a quantitative-escape condition, nor an arbitrary auxiliary vanishing sequence.

definitions.name: contrast-specific early-scale realized-QV Wald interval
definitions.construction:
For the prespecified nonzero \(c\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), use the early-scale event-truncated sandwich and define the total Wald interval
\[
 I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_T-z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T},\ 
 \widehat\tau_T+z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T}\right].
\]

definitions.name: early-stabilized projected adaptive IPW-Z class
definitions.construction:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\), the common objects \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho,\Theta\), deterministic tolerance sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), deterministic integers \(0\le k_T<T\), and deterministic numbers \(\omega_{c,T}>0\) satisfying
\[
 T\omega_{c,T}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac{k_T}{T\omega_{c,T}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let \((\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c))_{T\ge1}\) be any chosen sequence of law classes such that every \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score},
\]
\[
 \mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}.
\]
For each member law there must exist a positive random scale \(\Lambda_T\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\), such that \(\Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}\) almost surely and the chosen class sequence satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}projected\text{-}predictable\text{-}qv\text{-}growth}\). Here \(\mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}\) requires only \(T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\to0\); no unscaled convergence of \(r_T+\delta_T\) is imposed. No information-growth condition is imposed in a direction orthogonal to \(H^{-\top}c\), and neither finite attractors nor convergence of the full matrix \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) is required.

definitions.name: Saco enumerated AIPW class with early QV stabilization
definitions.construction:
For each row \(n\), let \(\mathcal T_n=\{t_{n,1}<\cdots<t_{n,N_n}\}\) be a deterministic scored set, fixed before data collection, and put \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}=|\mathcal T_n|\).  The class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}=(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}})_{n\ge1}\) consists of triangular arrays of binary-treatment laws with the following properties, imposed row by row and uniformly over the displayed class.

First, the source conditions retained from Saco are written out explicitly.  For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(Y_{n,t}(a)\) is the potential outcome depending only on the current treatment, and \(Y_{n,t}=A_{n,t}Y_{n,t}(1)+(1-A_{n,t})Y_{n,t}(0)\) almost surely.  The triples \((X_{n,t},Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\) are independent and identically distributed over \(t\) within a row and are unaffected by the adaptive policy.  There is a pre-treatment sigma-field \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), containing the past and \(X_{n,t}\), such that the logged propensity \(\pi_{n,t}\) is \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\)-measurable and
\[
0<\pi_{n,t}<1,\qquad
\mathbb P_n(A_{n,t}=1\mid\mathcal B_{n,t})=\pi_{n,t}\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), \(A_{n,t}\) is independent of \((Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\).  There is one constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) such that
\[
\epsilon\le\pi_{n,t}\le1-\epsilon
\quad\text{almost surely for every }t\in\mathcal T_n.
\]
For each \(a\), the fitted regression \(\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}\), as a random function, is measurable with respect to the history \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\).  There are finite constants \(C_Y,C_M\), common to the class, such that
\[
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t,a}E_{\mathbb P_n}|Y_{n,t}(a)|^4\le C_Y,\qquad
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t\in\mathcal T_n,a}
E_{\mathbb P_n}|\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}(X_{n,t})|^4\le C_M.
\]
Thus these are uniform versions of source Assumptions \(3.5,3.6,3.2,3.7,3.8,4.5,4.8,3.9,\) and \(3.10\), in the order specified by the directive.

Define the causal target, AIPW pseudo-outcome, centered score, estimator, and its sample variance by
\[
\theta_{0,n}=E_{\mathbb P_n}\{Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)\},
\]
\[
\widehat\phi_{n,t}=\frac{A_{n,t}}{\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})\}
-\frac{1-A_{n,t}}{1-\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t})\}
+\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t}),
\]
\[
X_{n,s}=\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\theta_{0,n},\qquad
S_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s},\qquad
Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s}^2,
\]
\[
\widehat\theta_n=N_n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}},\qquad
\widehat V_n=(N_n-1)^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}
\{\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\widehat\theta_n\}^2
\quad(N_n\ge2).
\]
To order the deterministic scored set without discarding interstitial history, define
\[
\mathcal G_{n,0}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,1}-1},\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,s}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s+1}-1}\ (1\le s<N_n),\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,N_n}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,N_n}}.
\]
Then \(X_{n,s}\) is \(\mathcal G_{n,s}\)-measurable and \(\mathcal G_{n,s-1}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s}-1}\).  Put
\[
V_n^2=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}].
\]
The source variance-growth Assumption \(5.11\) is retained: \(N_n\to\infty\), and for one \(v_->0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n(V_n^2<v_-N_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Finally, intersect those source conditions with early quadratic-variation stabilization.  There are deterministic integers \(0\le k_n<N_n\), a constant \(\lambda_->0\), and, for every member law, a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,k_n}\)-measurable random variable \(\Lambda_n\) such that
\[
\frac{k_n}{N_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \Lambda_n\ge\lambda_-\quad\text{almost surely},
\]
and, writing
\[
A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{s=k_n+1}^{N_n}
E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}],
\]
one has, for every \(\zeta>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n\left(\left|\frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\Lambda_n}-1\right|>\zeta\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}\) is exactly Saco's enumerated AIPW/DML class, with the overlap and fourth-moment constants made uniform across the triangular array, intersected with this early-measurable suffix-QV condition.  No almost-sure bound on \(X_{n,s}\) is imposed.

statements.statement:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_J\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is used.
statements.justification: This theorem derives predictable-QV control, exact-root localization, basin-conditional Gaussian limits, and the joint sigma(J)-stable Gaussian kernel from separated finite attractors and one common Cesaro modulus.
statements.gap: Guo and Xu prove ordinary Gaussian inference after inverse propensities stabilize and display two numerical modes; they do not prove a uniform finite-attractor stable kernel. Their bounded diagnostic analogue has two separated lock-in events but also a continuum of switching-surface equilibria, so it does not certify this class.
statements.consumer: A HeartSteps-style online learner can retain the deployment-selected basin in the asymptotic law for a prespecified causal excursion contrast without assuming pointwise convergence of the adaptive state.

statements.statement:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\]
Then \(J_T\) and \(\Lambda_T\) are \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, all early-scale conditions hold uniformly, and the same pivot and coverage conclusions follow.
statements.justification: An early-measurable directional information scale, a negligible prefix, bounded adaptive IPW scores, and \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) suffice for a total realized-QV pivot and uniform Wald coverage; the exact bounded Saco specialization shows that predictable-QV lower growth alone does not.
statements.gap: Saco, arXiv:2602.15559v1, Theorem 5.14, asserts a variance-growth-only Studentized central limit theorem. The bounded AIPW specialization in the counterexample proposition satisfies the published hypotheses and refutes that conclusion. This theorem supplies the missing early-measurability boundary, proves uniform exact-root localization and feasible square-root QV comparison, and makes truncation asymptotically inactive.
statements.consumer: For a HeartSteps-style causal excursion contrast fixed before analysis, inference remains valid when irrelevant score directions are weak, provided the target-direction suffix scale is early measurable and the prefix is negligible.

statements.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.
statements.justification: This theorem exactly characterizes every-level fixed-sandwich validity for one causal contrast under an arbitrary limiting covariance mixing law.
statements.gap: Directional-stability work gives sufficient target-specific conditions and Saco highlights random predictable variance; neither gives the general scale-mixture every-level converse.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can decide whether a deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other covariance directions remain random.

statements.statement:
Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.
statements.justification: This theorem separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance invariance for an arbitrary limiting covariance law.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from matrix stability on the sufficiency side; the general every-level necessity and finite-contrast polarization certificate remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software reporting many adaptive-experiment contrasts can determine whether one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.

statements.statement: For the augmented compact Markov chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\in\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\) generated by the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion, with initial slopes \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\), initialization \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\), and law \(P_{\eta_0}\), characterize the almost-sure limit set of the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\). In particular, determine whether there exist \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\ge1\), distinct deterministic states \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_1,\ldots,\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a tail-measurable \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\) such that \(P_{\eta_0}\{(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\to\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\}=1\) for every \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), with \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j\) if and only if the projected limit equals \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_j\). If this finite family exists, identify \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\), the projected limit states, and the initial-slope basins \(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\}\), and determine whether, for every compact \(K_0\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\operatorname{relint}_{\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j)\), there exist deterministic \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) satisfying \(\sup_{\eta_0\in K_0}P_{\eta_0}\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,2})^\top-\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\|_2>r_T(K_0)\}\le\delta_T(K_0)\). If finite projected tail selection fails, characterize the projected almost-sure limit set instead. Any ODE or stochastic-approximation reduction must be derived for the augmented chain and may not treat the slopes alone as Markov or \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) as invariant. This question concerns only the bounded-analogue dynamics and asserts neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference result must separately define \(g_{\mathrm{GX}}\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a unique \(\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), a nonzero \(c_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and \(\tau_{\mathrm{GX}}=c_{\mathrm{GX}}^\top\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and must verify every class assumption.
statements.justification: This dynamics-only question isolates the unverified premise behind the numerical two-mode example: finite almost-sure selection of projected slope limits and relative-basin-interior Cesaro attraction for a fully specified augmented bounded recursion.
statements.gap: Borkar gives local lock-in conditional on entry into an attraction domain, Pemantle gives unstable-point avoidance, and Guo--Xu Section 3.1 gives a Gaussian-noise simulation; none classifies the projected almost-sure limit set of the augmented chain or proves finite projected tail selection with relative-basin-interior uniform attraction for this bounded Rademacher analogue.
statements.consumer: A solution would determine the bounded analogue's operating regimes and state exactly what additional, separately specified causal-score verification would be required before any inference theorem could be invoked.

sampling_model.design: Known, logged, context-dependent randomization \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})=\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\) updated by a history-measurable recursion.
sampling_model.units: A growing sequence of independent full-data decision occasions \(W_t\); the inferential dependence is induced by the common adaptive policy state.
sampling_model.treatment: A finite action set with sequential randomization and consistency \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known clipping floor \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\), common over the triangular-array law class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No outcome-model nuisance is required for identification; a preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a total measurable exact-root selector, the Z-Jacobian and realized score quadratic variation are estimated on the observed adaptive path, and the sandwich is set to \(I_d\) off the common invertibility event.

estimand_functional: \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\},\quad P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c),\quad 0\le k_T<T,\quad \Lambda_T\text{ is positive and }\mathcal F_{k_T}\text{-measurable},\quad \Lambda_T\ge\omega_{c,T}>0,\quad T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty,\quad k_T/(T\omega_{c,T})\to0,\quad \{\sum_{t=k_T+1}^TE_P[(c^\top H^{-1}\xi_t)^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\}/(T\Lambda_T)\to_P 1\text{ uniformly},\quad \|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T),\quad\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\},\quad\widehat\theta_T=\begin{cases}\operatorname{lexmin}(\mathcal Z_T),&\text{on }E_T,\\\widetilde\theta_T,&\text{on }E_T^c,\end{cases}\quad\widehat\tau_T=c^\top\widehat\theta_T,\quad T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\quad\widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\quad\mathcal H_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\},\quad\widehat q_T(c)=\begin{cases}c^\top\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}c,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T,\\0,&\text{on }\mathcal H_T^c,\end{cases}\quad\mathcal E_T(c)=\mathcal H_T\cap\{\widehat q_T(c)\ge\omega_{c,T}/2\},\quad\widehat V_T(c)=\mathbf1_{\mathcal E_T(c)}\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}+\mathbf1_{\mathcal E_T(c)^c}I_d,\quad\sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0,\quad I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)=[\widehat\tau_T\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{c^\top\widehat V_T(c)c/T}],\quad\sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)|\to0\). Every \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\) admits the construction \(k_T=\min\{T-1,\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\rceil\}\), \(\Lambda_T=(H^{-\top}c)^\top\Omega_{J_T}H^{-\top}c\), and \(\omega_{c,T}=\omega_-\|c\|_2^2/(KD_1)^2\), where \(J_T\) is the early nearest-attractor label. Separately, for Saco's binary AIPW target \(\theta_{0,n}=E\{Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)\}\), Definition~\(\mathrm{def:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}class}\) fixes a deterministic scored set of size \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}\), \(k_n=o(N_n)\), a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,k_n}\)-measurable \(\Lambda_n\ge\lambda_->0\), and suffix predictable QV \(A_{n,+}^2/(N_n\Lambda_n)\to_P1\) uniformly; Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}pivot}\) delivers \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\), the feasible sample-variance Studentized limit, and Wald coverage uniformly on that intersection class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Saco's Theorem 5.14, equations (5.5)--(5.6), asserts realized-QV and feasible Studentized normality under its enumerated AIPW/DML assumptions and predictable-QV growth. The bounded specialization in \(\mathrm{prop:saco\text{-}theorem\text{-}5\text{-}14\text{-}counterexample}\) satisfies those hypotheses and refutes that conclusion; \(\mathrm{thm:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}pivot}\) proves the direct repair on the published class intersected with early QV stabilization.

Guo and Xu study a different decaying-overlap regime in which Gaussian IPW-Z conclusions require stabilization of scaled inverse propensities. Their numerical two-mode example motivates the basin question but proves neither the present finite-attractor class nor the early-scale projected class.

Shen and coauthors obtain target-specific normal inference under deterministic stability of a target-relevant direction. The present result uses an early-measurable random suffix scale and same-path self-normalization; the regimes and estimators are not known to be nested.
For generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, a continuous-state SDE invariant law controls optimal-arm pull proportions and nonstandard normalized-mean limits in the multiple-optimum regime.

Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study stationary-evaluation-policy off-policy M-estimation with flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging. Their class and target are not established to contain, or be contained in, the present early-scale adaptive IPW-Z class.

Conditional on entering an attraction domain, stochastic approximation locks into a prescribed stable equilibrium with an explicit high-probability bound; this does not by itself supply the present compact-uniform Cesaro modulus or early-scale suffix-QV approximation.

tldr: The field-tier contribution is a conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle for adaptive causal IPW-Z inference. Under common score, derivative, Jacobian-lower-bound, policy, covariance-lower-bound, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes, with attainable basins defined as the positive-mass support of the tail selector, the bundle derives a basin-stable finite Gaussian mixture with predictable-QV error controlled by \(r_T+\delta_T\), proves that an always-defined same-path realized-QV sandwich is uniformly pivotal and asymptotically untruncated, and gives exact deterministic-sandwich boundaries: every-level validity for one contrast holds if and only if that contrast's variance is basin-invariant, while validity for all contrasts holds if and only if the full covariance is deterministic. Theorem 2 has one direct strict-tightening comparator, Saco's pointwise realized-QV result; the remaining named papers provide motivation, ingredients, or orthogonal regimes rather than a second strict frontier. An elementary bounded two-basin law verifies that contrastwise invariance need not imply matrix invariance. The slope-projected limit set of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu Markov chain remains an open dynamics question with no class-membership or inference claim.

project_justification.gap: Saco supplies the one direct pointwise realized-QV comparator, but not uniform verification over an endogenous finite-attractor class. Guo--Xu and Shen and coauthors supply adjacent stable-policy and directional-stability results, Han studies continuous SDE-invariant Thompson-sampling pull proportions and raw-arm-mean inference, and Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study stationary-evaluation-policy off-policy M-estimation with flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy instead study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Existing stochastic-approximation results control lock-in only after entry into an attraction domain, and the Guo--Xu two-mode example remains numerical.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied field-tier object is a conditional recursion-level uniform limit theory that preserves the random basin, validates a finite-sample-defined same-path studentizer, and states exact contrastwise and matrixwise boundaries for deterministic-sandwich inference. The absence of a second direct strict-tightening comparator caps the positioning at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target.
project_justification.fill: The publishable contribution is the conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle: a basin-stable causal IPW-Z finite Gaussian mixture, a uniformly feasible same-path realized-QV pivot, and exact contrastwise and matrixwise deterministic-sandwich boundaries. A finite-attractor class indexed by common score, derivative, Jacobian lower, policy, covariance lower, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes converts policy dynamics into predictable-QV control with error \(r_T+\delta_T\); its attainable-basin index set is the positive-mass support of the tail selector. The score and derivative envelopes already imply \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) and \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\), so no primitive upper matrix bounds are imposed. The proposal-specific envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\) combines sampling, attraction, and approximation errors. A preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a compact empirical-root set; martingale concentration and a quantitative inverse-function argument make the exact-root selector active with probability tending uniformly to one. Stable martingale convergence supplies the mixture, event-truncated realized QV supplies the feasible pivot, finite normal-mixture identification plus polarization supplies the two necessity results, and a bounded in-class law certifies strict logical separation of the directional and matrix frontiers.

related_work: Guo and Xu, Theorems 3.2--3.3, prove marginal and joint IPW-Z Gaussian limits after scaled inverse propensities stabilize; their Section 3.1 no-intercept clipped-LinUCB example supplies numerical evidence of two modes, not a proved finite-attractor theorem or certification of the present class. Guo--Xu is an informed-by comparator. Saco, Theorem 5.14 and Design A in Section 6.6, establishes a pointwise realized-QV pivot under variance growth and illustrates random post-burn-in variance; Theorem 2 is the sole direct strict tightening, giving uniform validity over the conditional finite-attractor class and deriving truncation inactivity from common basin-covariance, attraction, and exact-root localization controls. The Abstract and Introduction of Shen and coauthors distinguish directional stability from full-matrix stability; that distinction informs Theorems 3--4, while the finite-basin every-level converses and bounded separation witness are not presented as a strict comparator chain. Han studies an orthogonal instability mechanism and target: for generalized Gaussian Thompson sampling, Proposition 2.6 and Theorem 2.7 on PDF pages 9--10, together with introduction equation (1.4) on page 4, identify the joint optimal-arm pull-proportion and noise limit with the unique invariant law of a continuous-state SDE. Han's Theorem 3.2 on PDF page 12 and introduction equation (1.5) on page 5 give Gaussian normalized-mean limits for stable arms and an SDE-defined semi-universal limit for multiple optimal arms; the body reports simulation evidence that the latter law is genuinely non-Gaussian, and Corollary 3.3 on PDF page 13 constructs confidence intervals from its quantiles. Han is close motivation, not a result anticipating Theorems 1--4 or the bounded Guo--Xu certification question. Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study off-policy M-estimation under working-model misspecification for adaptively collected bandit data. Their target is a projected solution under a stationary evaluation policy, and flexible variance stabilization permits unstable or nonconvergent logging policies; this is an informed-by comparator rather than a same-path-QV or finite-attractor result. Borkar supplies local lock-in bounds, and Pemantle supplies unstable-point avoidance, but neither certifies the bounded recursion. Aldous and Eagleson supply stable-convergence language. Mourrat supplies only the bounded-martingale central-limit and quadratic-variation ingredient. Teicher together with Andrews and Mallows supplies identification of centered normal scale mixtures. Qian and coauthors and Liao and coauthors define the HeartSteps causal-excursion consumer. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Thus the comparison supports a field-tier conditional theorem bundle, with Saco as its only strict-tightening comparator and no second strict frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The two slopes do not form a Markov state because clipped-UCB decisions also depend on the inverse ridge Gram coordinates. The open-ended question therefore concerns the slope projection of the augmented chain \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\) on \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}\); \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\) indexes only its initial slopes and is not an invariant chain state space. This bounded Rademacher recursion is not yet shown to have finite projected tail selection, a relative-basin-interior Cesaro attraction modulus, or any separately specified causal-score structure, so it is not claimed to belong to \(\mathfrak P_T\) and Theorems 1--2 are not claimed to apply. Optional Gaussian moment-extension subquestion: after the bounded-model dynamics are classified, determine whether the published Gaussian-noise recursion admits analogous dynamics under suitable moment controls. This optional subquestion is not a premise, deliverable, theorem, or part of the bounded-model open-ended question. Correct coverage at one isolated nominal level also does not identify the scale mixture: two unequal basin variances can be paired with a deterministic scale whose symmetric interval has the desired probability at that one level. Theorem 3 deliberately requires every nominal level.
honest_scope: The project establishes a field-tier inference frontier conditional on membership in the common-envelope finite-attractor class. Saco is the only direct strict-tightening comparator; the absence of a second direct strict frontier caps the contribution at field tier, which is the requested floor and achieved target. Guo--Xu, Shen and coauthors, Han, Leiner--Dunn--Ramdas, Borkar, and the remaining cited papers serve as informed-by comparators, ingredients, close motivation, or orthogonal regimes. The project treats a growing-horizon superpopulation adaptive experiment with a known randomization rule, not a pure fixed-finite-population randomization theorem. The bounded two-basin construction is solely an elementary, non-novel existence witness for strict logical separation between contrastwise and matrixwise invariance. It is not evidence that either the specified bounded Rademacher analogue or the published Gaussian no-intercept Guo--Xu recursion satisfies the finite-attractor, attraction, or common-envelope conditions. The open-ended question concerns only the slope-projected dynamics of the augmented bounded chain and does not assert membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) or applicability of Theorems 1--2. Any future inference theorem must separately specify its causal score, parameter space, unique target root, nonzero target contrast, induced scalar target, and every class assumption. The Gaussian moment extension remains optional and open. When \(m=1\), \(J=1\), \(V_J=V_1\) is deterministic, Theorem 1 is ordinary asymptotic normality, Theorem 2 is ordinary realized-QV studentization, and Theorems 3--4 allow \(\Sigma=V_1\).
